column5: The offline cart is cleared on login even when the server rejected some items so those items are lost
column6: syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:77-160 dispatches clearOfflineCart() at :110 as soon as response.success is true - before it inspects response.data.failed_items at :113. Items the server refused (out of stock - not sellable in the active market - variant gone) are therefore deleted from the only local copy the user has. The failed list is passed to a modal at :119 through the window global showFailedItemsModal - which is registered by src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 and DELETED again at :41 when that component unmounts - so if the modal is not mounted at that moment the guard at :115-118 is false and the user is told nothing at all. Either way the items are already gone from state and cannot be retried or recovered.
column10: User has items in the offline cart while logged out and at least one of them is rejected by the server on sync - for example an item that went out of stock or is not sellable in the active market.
column11: 1. While logged out add two products to the cart and let the offline cart persist. 2. Make one of them unsellable server side - out of stock or removed from the active market. 3. Log in and let the sync run. 4. Read the cart and the offline cart state.
column12: Rejected items stay in the offline cart (or are surfaced with a retry) so the customer keeps what they chose and can act on it.
column13: The whole offline cart is cleared regardless of failures. The failed items exist only inside a transient modal payload and are unrecoverable once it closes or if it never opened.
column14: Silent loss of items the customer deliberately added. The most likely moment for this is the login that happens at the start of checkout so it directly costs conversions and the customer may not notice items are missing before paying.
column15: Clear only the items the server accepted - keep any id present in failed_items in the offline cart - and surface the failure through normal React state rather than a window global that may not exist. Dispatch setOfflineCart with the remainder instead of clearOfflineCart.

column5: clampQuantity can return a quantity below the product minimum and its second branch is unreachable
column6: clampQuantity at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:55-85 first clamps into the min and max and stock window at :61-64 then snaps to the step size. The stepSize > 1 branch at :66-73 snaps to an absolute multiple of stepSize and never re-checks minQuantity - so a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2 given a desired quantity of 3 yields qty 3 at :61 - then remainder 3 % 2 = 1 at :67 - then qty = 2 at :69 - and the guard at :70 compares against stepSize rather than minQuantity so 2 is not raised back. The function returns 2 for a product whose minimum is 3. The else branch at :74-82 is dead code because it is reached only when stepSize is 1 (item.stepSize || 1 at :57 makes 0 impossible) and any value modulo 1 is 0 - so its remainder at :75 is always 0. Note the two branches also encode different models - absolute multiples in one and offsets from minQuantity in the other.
column10: A product configured with a minimum quantity above 1 and a step size above 1 where the minimum is not itself a multiple of the step.
column11: 1. Configure a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2. 2. While logged out add it to the cart with quantity 3. 3. Read the stored offline cart quantity.
column12: The quantity respects the product minimum and the step rule together - the nearest valid value at or above the minimum.
column13: The quantity is snapped down to 2 which is below the configured minimum of 3.
column14: Customer can build an offline cart that breaks the seller minimum order rule. It surfaces at login sync or at add-to-cart as a server rejection which then triggers the item loss described in issue 17.
column15: Snap to the step relative to minQuantity and re-clamp upward afterwards so the result is never below minQuantity - and delete the unreachable else branch so a single model applies.

column5: updateCartData decides the empty-cart case by string matching an English API message
column6: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:15-75 tests cartRes.message == 'Your cart is empty' at :49 to choose the empty-cart branch. CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids hard-coding status strings and the panel message is free text that other clients also consume. If the wording changes or is ever localised server side the comparison silently fails and control falls into the else at :59 which dispatches setError and raises a Cart Fetch Failed toast - so a normal empty cart is reported to the customer as a system failure and the checkout state is never reset by resetCheckOutState at :51.
column10: The panel returns success false with a message for the empty-cart case and that wording changes or is localised.
column11: 1. Empty the cart. 2. Change the panel message for the empty cart response or request it in a non English locale. 3. Reload the cart and read the UI.
column12: The empty cart renders the empty state and the checkout state is reset - keyed off a stable field such as a status code or an item count rather than prose.
column13: The empty cart is treated as a fetch failure - an error toast is shown and resetCheckOutState never runs so stale promo and wallet selections survive.
column14: A routine empty cart is presented as a broken page. Because resetCheckOutState is skipped a stale promo code or wallet flag can carry into the next order.
column15: Branch on a stable machine readable field - a status code or the item count on the payload - instead of the message text. If the panel has no such field request one and flag the contract gap rather than changing the shape unilaterally.

column5: Cart status toasts are hard-coded English and one contains a typo
column6: updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts raises four user-facing strings with no translation - title Cart is Empty and description Add Product to processed ! at :54-55 and title Cart Fetch Failed and description Could not update cart after adding item at :63-64. The same file uses i18n.t elsewhere for the sync toasts at :126-129 so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar. The description at :55 also reads Add Product to processed ! which is not grammatical English and appears to be intended as proceed.
column10: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any empty cart or failed cart refresh.
column11: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Empty the cart or force the cart refresh to fail. 3. Read the toast.
column12: The toast renders in the active language from the locale bundles.
column13: The toast renders in English in every language and shows the malformed sentence Add Product to processed !.
column14: Hindi and Arabic customers meet untranslated and grammatically broken English inside the cart which is a high intent part of the funnel.
column15: Move all four strings into the locale bundles under a cart namespace - fix the wording to proceed - add the keys to en hi and ar and run npm run scan:i18n.

column5: Merging two offline cart lines adds their quantities without applying the clamp so stock and maximum limits are bypassed
column6: updateOfflineCartItem at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:179-213 handles the case where editing addons changes an item id. When the new id already exists it merges with a bare addition at :198 - state.items[nextIndex].quantity += action.payload.newItem.quantity - and then splices the old line at :199. clampQuantity is never applied to that sum even though every other write path in the slice applies it - addOfflineCartItem at :126-129 and updateOfflineCartItemQuantity at :164-167 both clamp. The merged line can therefore exceed maxQuantity and exceed stock and can also break the step rule.
column10: Two offline cart lines for the same variant that differ only by addons where their combined quantity exceeds the stock or the maximum quantity.
column11: 1. While logged out add a product with addon set A and again with addon set B so two lines exist. 2. Edit one line so its addons match the other and the ids collide. 3. Read the merged quantity against the product stock and maximum.
column12: The merged quantity is clamped to the stock - maximum and step rules exactly as the other write paths clamp.
column13: The two quantities are summed unchecked so the line can exceed the stock and the maximum quantity.
column14: An offline cart that violates stock and quantity limits reaches the login sync and is rejected there - which then destroys the items through issue 17. The subtotal shown to the customer before login is also wrong.
column15: Apply clampQuantity to the summed quantity at :198 exactly as addOfflineCartItem does at :126-129 - ideally by routing every quantity write through one shared helper so a future path cannot skip it.

column5: Cart flows drive modals through a hidden DOM button click and a window global instead of React state
column6: Two cross-component signals in the cart path bypass React entirely. updateCartData at src/helpers/updators.ts:47 calls document.getElementById('removed-items-modal-open')?.click() to open the removed-items notice - the target is a hidden button rendered by src/components/Modals/RemovedItemsModal.tsx:62 and read back at :40. syncOfflineCartToServer at src/helpers/updators.ts:115-119 calls the window global showFailedItemsModal which src/components/Modals/FailedItemsModal.tsx:33 assigns on mount and deletes at :41 on unmount - and the call is cast through (window as any) which also breaches the no any rule in CLAUDE.md section 5. Both signals fail silently when the target component is not mounted and neither is type checked.
column10: The modal component is not mounted on the current route when the signal fires.
column11: 1. Trigger a cart refresh that returns removed_count above zero or a login sync that returns failed_items on a route where the matching modal is not mounted. 2. Observe that nothing opens and no error is raised.
column12: Cross-component signals travel through React state or a store so they are type checked and cannot be lost.
column13: The click target or the window function is absent so the notification is dropped without any diagnostic.
column14: The customer is never told that items were removed from the cart or rejected during sync. It also makes the flow untestable and invisible to the type checker.
column15: Replace both with state - a store flag or a context that the modals subscribe to - so the signal is typed and survives regardless of mount order. This also removes the two (window as any) casts.
